title: Worktrees
one_liner: A git worktree gives each Claude Code session its own files and branch on shared history, so parallel sessions and subagents do not overwrite each other.

core.title: One session, one worktree
core.body: A worktree is a separate working directory and branch that shares the repository history. Each session in its own worktree edits its own copy of the files.
core.why: Two sessions editing one checkout produce conflicting changes.

quotes.text: Running each Claude Code session in its own worktree gives it a separate copy of the files to edit
quotes.label: Worktrees

core.title: Start with --worktree
core.body: `claude --worktree <name>` (or `-w`) creates `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` on a new branch `worktree-<name>` and starts the session there. You can also ask Claude to 'work in a worktree' mid-session.
core.why: A single flag gives full isolation; no manual git commands are needed.

quotes.text: Pass `--worktree` or `-w` with a name to create an isolated worktree and start Claude in it.
quotes.label: Worktrees > Start Claude in a worktree

quotes.text: Add `.claude/worktrees/` to your `.gitignore` so worktree contents don't appear as untracked files in your main checkout.
quotes.label: Worktrees > Start Claude in a worktree

core.title: A worktree is a fresh checkout
core.body: Dependencies and gitignored files such as `.env` are not present. Install dependencies in the worktree, or list files to copy in a `.worktreeinclude` file.
core.why: Builds and tests fail in a new worktree until the environment is set up.

quotes.text: A worktree is a fresh checkout, so initialize your development environment there
quotes.label: Worktrees > Set up the environment

core.title: Isolation is enforced, with a gap
core.body: In a worktree session, Claude Code blocks edits, command working directories and git redirects that target the main checkout. It does not track files a shell command writes, so `cp` or a redirect into the main checkout is not blocked by these checks.
core.why: Treat isolation as protection for normal edits, not a sandbox.

quotes.text: Claude Code blocks an `Edit`, `Write`, or `NotebookEdit` that targets a path in the main checkout.
quotes.label: Worktrees > Enforcing isolation

quotes.text: None of them tracks which files a shell command writes
quotes.label: Worktrees > Enforcing isolation

core.title: Subagents can each get a worktree
core.body: Ask Claude to 'use worktrees for your agents', or add `isolation: worktree` to a subagent's frontmatter. A subagent worktree with no changes is removed automatically.
core.why: Parallel subagents that edit files need the same isolation as parallel sessions.

quotes.text: by adding `isolation: worktree` to its frontmatter.
quotes.label: Worktrees > Isolate subagents

quotes.text: Claude Code removes automatically when the subagent finishes without changes
quotes.label: Worktrees > Isolate subagents

core.title: Some things are shared with the main checkout
core.body: The `.git` directory, project-scope plugins, 'don't ask again' permission approvals, and untracked skills, agents and commands (when the worktree has none of its own).
core.why: An approval granted in one worktree applies to every worktree of the repository.

quotes.text: git commands in a worktree write to the main repository's shared `.git` directory
quotes.label: Worktrees > What is shared

practice.title: Run two isolated sessions
practice.goal: See parallel edits on separate branches.
steps: Ask each session to edit the same file differently
practice.check: `git worktree list` shows both worktrees, and `git branch` shows `worktree-feature-a` and `worktree-feature-b` with separate changes.
practice.variation: Omit the name and note the generated one.

practice.title: Make a subagent always isolate
steps: Create `.claude/agents/refactorer.md` with `isolation: worktree` in the frontmatter
Ask Claude to use the refactorer for a small rename
Run `git worktree list` while it runs
practice.check: A temporary worktree appears and the main checkout is unchanged.
practice.variation: Ask for a change that produces no diff and confirm the worktree is removed.

gotchas: Interactive `--worktree` runs need workspace trust; run `claude` once in the directory first.
`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in hooks stays at the original project root after entering a worktree; read `cwd` from the hook input instead.
If `permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories` is on, Claude has no `EnterWorktree` tool; start with `claude --worktree` instead.

recall.q: Where does `claude --worktree x` create the worktree?
Why might tests fail in a new worktree?
recall.a: It is a fresh checkout without dependencies or gitignored files.

recall.q: Which writes to the main checkout are not blocked?
recall.a: Files written by shell commands such as `cp` or redirects, without git.

recall.q: What happens to a subagent worktree with no changes?
Name two things shared with the main checkout.
recall.a: The `.git` directory and 'don't ask again' approvals (also project plugins and untracked skills).
